title: MCAS trusted one sensor; redundancy is an architecture
body: Investigations of the 737 MAX accidents found the original MCAS could command nose-down trim from a single angle-of-attack sensor's faulty reading, repeatedly. Aviation's own tradition is dissimilar redundancy for flight-critical inputs. The redesign compares both sensors and limits authority. The core lesson predates software: never let one instrument be both judge and executioner.
